## Quick Answer

**Transistor 9.4/10** — Transistor is the best podcast hosting platform for professional podcasters, businesses, and creators who need unlimited shows on a single account, advanced analytics, and indie-friendly customer support. With over 20,000 podcast feeds hosted, plans starting at $19/month, and a 25% monthly recurring affiliate commission, Transistor stands out for its no-nonsense approach to podcast hosting.

The standout features are **unlimited podcasts on every plan** (no extra per-show fees), **video podcast hosting** with auto-posting to YouTube, **private podcasting** for internal communications and paid subscriber feeds, and **IAB-certified analytics** that advertisers trust. Transistor is built by an independent team (founders Justin Jackson and Jon Buda) and has earned a reputation for genuinely responsive human support.

If you're looking for a podcast host that treats you like a partner rather than a number, Transistor is absolutely worth your consideration in 2026.

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Unlimited podcasts on every plan** — No per-show fees, no limits on how many shows you can host. This saves serious money for networks and multi-show creators.
- **Video podcast hosting** — Upload video episodes and auto-distribute to YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts. This is a relatively new and powerful feature that many competitors still lack.
- **IAB-certified analytics** — Transistor's download numbers are certified by the IAB Tech Lab, meaning advertisers and sponsors trust them. This is critical for monetization.
- **Private podcasting done right** — Create members-only feeds for Patreon supporters, internal training for teams, or paid subscriber content. Works seamlessly with existing membership platforms.
- **Indie-owned with real human support** — Founded by Justin Jackson and Jon Buda, Transistor is independently owned. Support is handled by actual humans who respond quickly and know the product inside out.
- **No hidden fees** — What you see on the pricing page is what you pay. No surprise overage charges, no enterprise upsells hiding behind fine print.
- **Built-in podcast website** — Every show gets a customizable website with its own URL, embeddable player, and automatic episode listing. No design skills needed.
- **Dynamic ad insertion** — The Professional and Business plans include dynamic ad placement (pre-roll, mid-roll, post-roll) so you can monetize without editing episodes manually.

### Cons 👎

- **Higher entry price** — At $19/month, Transistor costs more than Buzzsprout ($12/mo) and Podbean ($9/mo). The free tier only gives you 14 days (not 90 days like Buzzsprout's free trial).
- **No Magic Mastering / audio enhancement** — Unlike Buzzsprout's AI-powered audio enhancement, Transistor doesn't offer built-in audio mastering. You'll need a separate tool like Auphonic or Descript.
- **No built-in monetization marketplace** — Buzzsprout has an Affiliate Marketplace that connects podcasters with sponsors. Transistor doesn't have this — you need to find your own sponsors.
- **Starter plan caps at 20K downloads** — Growing podcasts will quickly need to upgrade to the Professional plan, which is $49/month — a significant jump.
- **No free plan** — Unlike Spotify for Creators (free) or Buzzsprout (limited free uploads), Transistor only offers a 14-day free trial. After that, you're paying.

---

## Who Is Transistor For?

### Ideal For ✅

- **Professional podcasters** — Those running multiple shows and needing a reliable, no-fuss host with unlimited shows
- **Businesses and organizations** — Internal communications via private podcasts, training content, and brand shows
- **Podcast networks** — Managing multiple shows under one account is a massive time and cost saver
- **Creators who value indie ethics** — If supporting independent businesses matters to you, Transistor's indie ownership is a genuine differentiator
- **Video podcasters** — The new video hosting + YouTube auto-publish feature is excellent for expanding reach
- **Paid subscriber content creators** — Private podcast feeds integrate smoothly with membership platforms like Patreon, Memberful, and Supercast

### Not Ideal For ❌

- **Complete beginners on a tight budget** — The $19/month starting price and lack of a free plan make it less accessible than Buzzsprout or Spotify for Creators
- **Podcasters who want AI audio mastering** — If you need one-click audio enhancement, Buzzsprout's Magic Mastering is better
- **Monetization-first creators** — Buzzsprout's Affiliate Marketplace gives you a faster path to sponsorship revenue
- **High-volume podcasts over 250K downloads** — Enterprise pricing at $199+/month is expensive, and few alternatives exist at that scale

---

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### 1. Unlimited Podcast Hosting

Transistor's headline feature is that every plan — even the $19/month Starter — includes unlimited podcast shows. This is rare in the industry. Buzzsprout charges per show (additional shows cost extra), and most competitors limit you to one show on entry-level plans.

This makes Transistor uniquely valuable for:
- **Agencies** managing client podcasts
- **Media companies** running multiple branded shows
- **Educators** creating separate series for different courses
- **Hobbyists** who want to experiment with multiple topics

Each show gets its own RSS feed, analytics dashboard, and podcast website. Reordering episodes, editing metadata, and managing multiple publishing schedules are all handled from a single clean interface.

### 2. Video Podcast Hosting

Transistor added native video podcast support in 2025, and it's been a game-changer. You can upload MP4 files directly to Transistor, and the platform handles distribution to YouTube, Spotify (which now supports video), and Apple Podcasts.

Key video features:
- Upload up to 8GB per video episode (Business plan)
- Automatic YouTube publishing — once connected, new video episodes go live on YouTube without manual upload
- Cross-platform stats — see how your video episodes perform on YouTube vs. audio-only platforms
- Video embeddable player for your website
- Episode artwork generator for video thumbnails

This eliminates the need for a separate YouTube publishing workflow, which saves hours per week for active podcasters.

### 3. Private Podcasting

Transistor offers the most mature private podcasting feature in the industry. Private podcasts let you create an audio (or video) feed that requires authentication to access.

Common use cases:
- **Internal company communications** — CEOs sending weekly updates, HR training, all-hands meetings
- **Paid subscriber feeds** — Connect with Patreon, Memberful, Supercast, or WordPress plugins
- **Course content** — Deliver lesson audio to students via their podcast app
- **Sales enablement** — Share prospect-specific content with individualized feeds

The private podcast subscriber limits are generous: 50 on Starter, 500 on Professional, 3,000 on Business. Enterprise plans handle unlimited subscribers.

### 4. IAB-Certified Analytics

Transistor's analytics are certified by the IAB Tech Lab — the industry standard for podcast measurement. This matters because:
- **Advertisers trust IAB-certified numbers** — If you're selling sponsorships, your download counts are credible
- **Accurate listener data** — Transistor filters out bots and duplicate downloads using IAB v2.0 guidelines
- **Granular reporting** — See downloads by episode, geographic location, podcast app, and time period
- **Trend analysis** — Track subscriber growth, episode performance trends, and audience retention
- **Exportable reports** — Download CSV data for your own analysis or ad decks

You can see exactly which apps your listeners use (Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Overcast, etc.), which countries they're in, and how your episodes trend over time.

### 5. Dynamic Ad Insertion

Available on Professional ($49/mo) and Business ($99/mo) plans, Transistor's dynamic ad insertion lets you:
- Create pre-roll, mid-roll, and post-roll ad slots
- Swap ads dynamically — update an old episode's ad without re-uploading
- Target ads to specific episodes or date ranges
- Track ad impressions with IAB-certified stats

This is essential for monetized podcasts. Instead of editing audio files every time you get a new sponsor, you inject ads at the server level. Old episodes automatically serve the latest ad.

### 6. Integrations and API

Transistor connects with your existing workflow through:
- **Zapier** — Automate episode publishing, notifications, and CRM updates
- **API Access** — Full REST API for programmatic episode management, analytics retrieval, and subscriber management
- **WordPress plugins** — Several third-party plugins integrate Transistor RSS feeds into WordPress sites
- **Webhooks** — Trigger custom actions when new episodes are published
- **Podcast Standards Project membership** — Transistor is a founding member, ensuring compatibility with open podcasting standards

### 7. Website Builder and Embeddable Player

Every Transistor show gets a professional website at no extra cost. Features include:
- Customizable themes and colors
- Episode listing with audio/video player
- Subscribe buttons for all major podcast apps
- SEO-friendly URLs and meta tags
- Optional custom domain

The embeddable player works anywhere — WordPress, Squarespace, Carrd, or your own HTML site. It supports both audio and video, and shows episode artwork, descriptions, and timestamps.

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose the Right Podcast Host

Choosing a podcast host is one of the most important decisions you'll make as a podcaster. Here's what to consider:

### 1. Download Limits vs. Upload Limits

Some podcast hosts limit how many downloads you can have (Transistor, Captivate) while others limit how many hours you can upload (Buzzsprout). If you produce short episodes with high download numbers, Transistor's model works better. If you produce long-form content with moderate audience size, Buzzsprout's upload cap model is more cost-effective.

### 2. How Many Shows Do You Run?

If you're running multiple podcasts, Transistor's unlimited-shows-on-every-plan model is significantly cheaper than competitors that charge per show. Buzzsprout, for example, charges $12/month for your first show and additional shows cost extra.

### 3. Do You Need Video?

Transistor's native video podcast support with auto-YouTube publishing is a powerful feature that only a handful of hosts offer natively. If video is part of your strategy — and it should be in 2026 — prioritize hosts with good video support.

### 4. Monetization Path

How do you plan to make money? If you want an integrated sponsorship marketplace, Buzzsprout is better. If you're building a paid subscriber community, Transistor's private podcasting with membership integrations is ideal. If you're selling ads yourself, Transistor's dynamic ad insertion on higher plans makes that easier.

### 5. Analytics Credibility

For anyone serious about monetization, IAB-certified analytics are non-negotiable. Ad buyers require them. Transistor, Buzzsprout, and Captivate all offer IAB-certified analytics. Some cheaper hosts (Podbean's lower tiers, Spotify for Creators) do not.

### 6. Support Quality

All podcast hosts claim great support. Transistor genuinely delivers — their team is known in the podcasting community for quick, human responses. If you value being able to talk to the people who built the product, Transistor and Buzzsprout both excel here.

---

## Competitor Comparisons

### Transistor vs. Buzzsprout

This is the most common comparison in podcast hosting. Buzzsprout is better for beginners with its Magic Mastering (AI audio enhancement), 90-day free trial (vs. Transistor's 14 days), and built-in Affiliate Marketplace for sponsor discovery. Transistor wins on unlimited shows, private podcasting depth, and video hosting with auto-YouTube publish.

**Choose Buzzsprout if:** You're a solo podcaster starting out, want AI audio enhancement, and value the longer free trial.
**Choose Transistor if:** You run multiple shows, need private podcasting for paid subscribers, or want native video podcast hosting.

### Transistor vs. Captivate

Captivate is the closest direct competitor to Transistor. Both offer unlimited shows on all plans, IAB-certified analytics, and similar pricing ($19-$99/mo). Captivate differentiates with built-in growth tools (like audiogram creation and transcription included). Transistor differentiates with private podcasting, video hosting, and a stronger indie ethos.

**Choose Captivate if:** You want included transcription and growth tools without add-ons.
**Choose Transistor if:** Private podcasting and video distribution are priorities for you.

### Transistor vs. Podbean

Podbean is the budget option, starting at $9/month. It offers unlimited bandwidth on most plans but lacks the polish and support quality of Transistor. Podbean's analytics are not IAB-certified on lower tiers, and the interface feels dated.

**Choose Podbean if:** You're on a very tight budget and just want your audio on platforms.
**Choose Transistor if:** You value quality analytics, responsive support, and a modern interface.

### Transistor vs. Spotify for Creators (formerly Anchor)

Spotify for Creators is completely free, which is tempting. But you trade freedom for that free price — limited analytics, less control over your RSS feed, and monetization heavily favoring Spotify. Many podcasters who start on Anchor eventually migrate to Transistor or Buzzsprout for more control.

**Choose Spotify for Creators if:** You're experimenting with podcasting and have zero budget.
**Choose Transistor if:** You're serious about podcasting and want ownership of your content and data.

### Transistor vs. Libsyn

Libsyn is the old guard — founded in 2004, it's been around since podcasting's early days. It offers reliable hosting and IAB-certified stats, but the interface is dated, storage-based pricing is confusing, and support is slower. Transistor offers a cleaner, more modern experience.

**Choose Libsyn if:** You want the longest track record and don't mind an older interface.
**Choose Transistor if:** You want a modern platform with better features and pricing.

## 7 Tips for Getting the Most Out of Transistor

1. **Start with the yearly plan** — The 12-for-10 pricing saves 17% and makes the $19/month Starter plan cost just $15.83/month. If you're committed to podcasting, it's a no-brainer.

2. **Use the embeddable player on your website** — Transistor's player is sleek, loads fast, and doesn't slow your site down. Embed it on your blog posts to increase episode engagement.

3. **Connect YouTube on day one** — If you're on the Professional plan or above, enable auto-YouTube posting immediately. Each video episode gets published to YouTube automatically, expanding your reach without extra work.

4. **Implement private podcasts for paid subscribers** — If you have a Patreon, Memberful, or similar membership platform, set up a private feed. Your supporters get episodes in their podcast app automatically, which increases retention.

5. **Leverage the API for automation** — If you're technically inclined, Transistor's REST API lets you automate episode publishing, pull analytics into your own dashboards, and manage subscribers programmatically.

6. **Use dynamic ads from episode one** — Even if you don't have sponsors yet, set up ad slots in your episodes. When you land a sponsor, you can insert their ad into old episodes without re-editing or re-uploading.

7. **Monitor analytics trends, not just raw numbers** — Pay attention to which apps your listeners use, which episodes retain best, and where your audience is geographically. These insights help you optimize content and pitch more effectively to sponsors.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Transistor and how does it work?

Transistor is a podcast hosting and analytics platform that lets you upload, distribute, and analyze your podcast episodes. You upload your audio (or video) files, Transistor generates an RSS feed and distributes it to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, and other directories. It also provides detailed analytics, a podcast website, and monetization features like dynamic ad insertion and private podcast feeds.

### How much does Transistor cost?

Transistor offers four plans: Starter at $19/month (20K downloads, unlimited shows), Professional at $49/month (100K downloads, dynamic ads, video), Business at $99/month (250K downloads, remove branding), and Enterprise at $199+/month. Yearly billing gives you 12 months for the price of 10. All plans include a 14-day free trial with no credit card required.

### Does Transistor offer unlimited podcast hosting?

Yes. Every Transistor plan includes unlimited podcasts — you can host as many shows as you want on a single account. This is one of Transistor's strongest differentiators, as most competitors charge per show or limit you to one show on entry-level plans.

### Does Transistor support video podcasting?

Yes. Transistor added native video podcast hosting in 2025. You can upload MP4 video files and distribute them to YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts. Professional and Business plans include auto-publishing to YouTube, meaning your video episodes go live on YouTube without manual upload.

### Can I create private podcasts with Transistor?

Absolutely. Transistor offers the best private podcasting feature in the industry. You can create password-protected feeds for internal team communications, paid subscriber content, or exclusive member benefits. Private subscriber limits range from 50 (Starter) to unlimited (Enterprise), with deep integrations for Patreon, Memberful, Supercast, and more.

### How do Transistor's analytics work?

Transistor provides IAB v2.0 certified analytics, meaning download counts are verified by the industry standard. You can see downloads by episode, geographic location, listening app, and time period. The analytics filter out bots and duplicate downloads automatically. You can also export reports as CSV for investor or sponsor decks.

### Does Transistor have a free plan?

No. Transistor only offers a 14-day free trial. After the trial, you must choose a paid plan. This is different from competitors like Buzzsprout (which offers limited free hosting) and Spotify for Creators (fully free).

### What integrations does Transistor support?

Transistor integrates with Zapier for workflow automation, has a full REST API for custom integrations, supports webhooks for event-driven actions, and includes compatible WordPress plugins. It's also a member of the Podcast Standards Project, supporting open podcasting standards.

### Is Transistor good for businesses?

Yes. Businesses use Transistor for internal communications (private podcasts), branded external shows, training content, and thought leadership podcasts. The unlimited shows feature is especially valuable for agencies managing multiple client podcasts, and the IAB-certified analytics provide credible metrics for reporting.

### How does Transistor compare to Buzzsprout?

Transistor and Buzzsprout are the top two recommended podcast hosts in 2026. Transistor wins on unlimited shows, private podcasting, and video hosting. Buzzsprout wins on beginner-friendliness, AI audio mastering (Magic Mastering), a longer free trial (90 days), and a built-in Affiliate Marketplace for finding sponsors. Both have excellent support — Transistor is more indie-oriented, Buzzsprout is more beginner-focused.

### Can I switch to Transistor from another podcast host?

Yes. Transistor offers migration assistance. You can import your existing episodes via RSS feed import, and the team helps ensure your redirects are properly set up so you don't lose subscribers. The process typically takes 24-48 hours for a smooth transition.

### Do I own my content on Transistor?

100%. You retain full ownership of all content you upload to Transistor. You can export your episodes and leave at any time. There are no lock-in contracts — all plans are month-to-month or annual (prepaid), and you're free to cancel anytime.

---

## Conclusion

Transistor is a premium podcast hosting platform that earns its reputation through reliability, transparency, and genuinely excellent support. It's not the cheapest option, and it's not the most beginner-friendly — but for anyone who's serious about podcasting, especially those running multiple shows or building a paid subscriber community, it's arguably the best choice available.

**The bottom line:** If you're a solo podcaster just starting out with a single show and a tight budget, Buzzsprout's $12/month plan with 90-day free trial is less risky. But if you're running multiple shows, want video podcasting with auto-YouTube distribution, need private podcast feeds, or simply value supporting an indie company that treats customers like partners — get Transistor.
